test_title: PYST 28: SSC GD Constable 2025 - English (Held On: 18 Feb, 2025 - Shift 1)
subject: english
question: Identify the sentence with the INCORRECT usage of an adverb.

options.text: Nila arrives always on time for meetings.
Nila never arrives on time for meetings.
Nila hardly ever arrives on time for meetings.
Nila usually arrives on time for meetings.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adverb "**always**" is incorrectly placed in the sentence. In English, adverbs of frequency (e.g., always, never, usually) are generally placed before the main verb.
 
• The correct placement should be: "Nila **always arrives** on time for meetings."
 
• Option 2 ("Nila never arrives on time for meetings."), Option 3 ("Nila hardly ever arrives on time for meetings."), and Option 4 ("Nila usually arrives on time for meetings.") use the adverbs correctly.
 
• Thus, the error is in **Option 1**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Nila always arrives on time for meetings."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Nila never arrives on time for meetings." – This is grammatically correct, as the adverb "never" is correctly placed before the verb "arrives."
 
• **Option 3:** "Nila hardly ever arrives on time for meetings." – This is grammatically correct, as the adverb phrase "hardly ever" is correctly placed before the verb "arrives."
 
• **Option 4:** "Nila usually arrives on time for meetings." – This is grammatically correct, as the adverb "usually" is correctly placed before the verb "arrives."
